findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the paper towel dispenser at the juice hand washing station to be non-operational. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) informed maintenance, who cleared the jam in the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always readily available to complete proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The standing cooler in the sampling prep room does not have an ambient thermometer. Ensure ambient thermometers are present at the front of cooling units to monitor the warmest temperature of the unit- which should be at or below 41F. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed fragmented caulking behind the hand washing sink of the juice station. Maintain proper repair of physical facilities by resealing the sink to the wall by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed food handler donning gloves before handling food. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the need to wash hands prior to donning gloves. Ensure all employees wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Sanitizer bottles were observed on the same shelf as the sampling orange juice on the cart. CORRECTED- employee moved the sampling juice to the counter. Education was provided regarding the need to separate toxic substances from ready to eat (RTE) food items. Ensure chemicals are stored away from RTE items to prevent potential contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Ice and juice was observed in the basin of the juicing station handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure handsinks are only used for handwashing (not used as a dump sink).
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: One of the 3 employees present during this inspection has not completed food handler training. PIC discussed the training with the employee and checked that they have access to the training in the computer-based learning system. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Spray bottle of sanitizer at both demo stations was observed at 0ppm quat. No sanitizer concentration could be detected from the wall-mounted dispenser at the 3 compartment sink, where both bottles would have been filled. PIC has contacted EcoLab to have them look at the wall-mounted dispenser. In the meantime, Crossmark staff will fill sanitizer spray bottles and do the few dishes they have to wash/rinse/sanitize at the 3 compartment sink in the Cafe.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration. [P]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
A food handler certificate was not available for one of the two employees serving samples during this inspection. Ensure all food employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire (and renew as needed). Keep certificates available on file for review during health inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]
